msg: Hola, buen día. Somos un grupo de 7 amigas de Bogotá. Tres ya tenemos el Open Water, dos quieren probar el minicurso y dos prefieren snorkel. ¿Cuánto saldría por persona saliendo desde Cartagena y hay descuento por grupo?
reply:
¡Hola! 🪸 Soy *Coral*, de *Diving Planet* — buceamos todo el año en las Islas del Rosario, saliendo desde Cartagena o desde las propias islas. 🌊

¡Buen día! ¡Qué chévere plan para las siete! Sí, pueden combinar buceo para certificadas, minicurso y snorkel en la misma salida; si hay poca gente, van juntas en la lancha, y si no, se organizan por actividad.

Como son de Bogotá, los precios son en COP. Te dejo a continuación los valores por persona para el minicurso y el snorkel saliendo desde Cartagena. Para las tres buzas certificadas, el plan desde Cartagena es de dos inmersiones; el sistema te deja también ese precio a continuación.

Sí hay descuento para grupos de cinco o más: se suma al descuento online en las actividades elegibles. Hay que solicitarlo antes de pagar; no aplica a cursos PADI.

*Precios por persona* (online · normal):
*Desde Cartagena* — lancha desde el Muelle de la Bodeguita · con almuerzo
• Minicurso de Buceo: 655.000 COP · 727.000 COP
• Tour de Snorkeling: 448.000 COP · 497.000 COP
*Ya en las Islas del Rosario* — recogida en tu hotel si tiene acceso por lancha · sin almuerzo
• Minicurso de Buceo: 475.000 COP · 528.000 COP
• Tour de Snorkeling: 150.000 COP · 167.000 COP

No hay descuento ni tarifa especial por ser colombiano: el precio es el mismo, solo cambia la moneda (COP).

Entonces, ¿saldrías *desde Cartagena* (Muelle de la Bodeguita)? 🚤

msg: Hello. My wife and I arrive on a cruise ship in Cartagena on March 3rd, docking at 7:00 am and we must be back on board by 5:00 pm. We would both like to snorkel. Is that doable? We are from Canada.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Snorkeling in the Rosario Islands is a lovely day trip, but the standard tour won’t fit your cruise schedule: it departs Cartagena at 8:00 a.m. and returns around 4:15 p.m., leaving too little time to get back on board by 5:00 p.m. The departure time is fixed, so I can’t confirm that it would work with your 7:00 a.m. docking.

So, would you leave *from Cartagena* (Muelle de la Bodeguita)? 🚤

Currency: Colombians (wherever they live) and residents of Colombia pay in COP and everyone else in USD; it is the same price in both currencies. Diving Planet policies:
- Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). The refresher is also 18 hours: it is for certified divers, even though it is booked as the mini course. The hours count from the last dive, not from the return to Cartagena. The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.
- If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
- For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
- Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 AM. Departing from Cartagena there is no hotel pick-up: each person gets to the dock on their own (ground transportation to the dock is not included).
- By booking you accept our terms and conditions, cancellation policy, and data treatment. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Date changes are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Changes to the number of people on a booking you already made are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Colombians (anyone with Colombian nationality, holding a Colombian cédula or passport, wherever they live; also dual nationals when one nationality is Colombian) and residents of Colombia (holders of a cédula de extranjería, a resident ID; living in Colombia without one is not enough) pay in Colombian pesos (COP). Saying they are Colombian or from a Colombian city ("I'm from Cali") already says it; what is not enough is only having been born there while living abroad: then ask whether they hold Colombian nationality or a cédula de extranjería. All other international clients pay in US dollars (USD). A group does not pay in parts: if the same booking mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group pays in US dollars (USD), residents and Colombians included. A Colombian together with someone who holds a cédula de extranjería, wherever they are from, is not a mixed group: both pay in pesos (COP). The price is the same: only the currency changes (there is no discount for being Colombian).
- If the group mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group booking is paid in US dollars (USD), at the same equivalent price. Someone with a cédula de extranjería does not count as a foreigner, wherever they are from. There is no different price for being Colombian.
- If you are already on the Rosario Islands, we coordinate pick-up and drop-off from hotels with maritime access. In some cases the boat arrives directly at the hotel; in others we indicate the nearest dock or meeting point.
- These plans have different prices because they do not include transport from Cartagena or lunch.
- Pick-up is only on the Rosario Islands: Barú (including Playa Blanca, which is on Barú) is not part of the islands and we do not operate or pick up there; guests staying in Barú depart from Cartagena (Muelle de la Bodeguita).
- It depends on the activity: snorkeling from 6 years old; Bubble Makers from 8 to 10 years old (pool mini-course and very shallow water practice, max 2 meters); the dive mini-course and the Open Water course from 10 years old; the Advanced course and the Rescue course from 12. Minors must be accompanied by a demonstrable parent or responsible relative.
- The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
- If you are a certified diver, there are no additional medical restrictions; your liability waiver is the certified-diver one: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). For the refresher day this one is not used: use the course medical form.
- Bringing or drinking alcohol on the boat or during the activity is not allowed, and no alcohol or other substances may be consumed before diving. You must be in good physical condition.
- The booking system on our website. It automatically closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you can no longer book for the next day, and you still book on the website for the next available day.
- To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
- From Cartagena: departure at 8:00 a.m. from Muelle de la Bodeguita and return at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.). From the islands: hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (8:00 a.m. for specialties and 7:30 a.m. on day 2 of some courses). Daytime activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m. (see the activity schedule). Night diving: in the evening (pick-up around 5:30 p.m., back around 7:30 p.m.). Online booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before; after that, you book on the website for the next available day.
- We only close on December 25 and January 1. The rest of the year we operate every day, including public holidays, except for suspension due to adverse weather conditions.
- The tour includes water all day, coconut candy between dives, and lunch (rice with chicken or rice with vegetables). The menu is always the same, it does not change by day/supplier. Vegetarians, vegans, and celiacs receive rice with vegetables. Guests may bring their own food if needed (e.g. allergy or special diet). If the guest has a food allergy, they must inform us before the tour. In multi-day packages departing from Cartagena, lunch is included on the first day only; plans for guests already on the islands do not include lunch.
- Photos and videos are not offered proactively or included in the price. The instructor may take them voluntarily and delivers them by the next day at the latest. Any tip to the instructor for photos/videos is voluntary: each guest gives whatever they like, directly to them. This applies to every activity, including the mini-course (and the refresher, booked as a mini-course), PADI courses and certified-diver trips: not included, the instructor may take them voluntarily.
- The 3, 4, 5, 7 and 9 dive packages are exclusively for certified divers with a minimum Open Water level. They are not available for uncertified beginners.
- Two-day courses (Open Water, Referral Course, Advanced, Rescue and Mindful Diving) require accommodation on the islands: at least one night, the night of day 1 (there is no return to Cartagena on day 1). There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel. The same goes for multi-day dive packages (4, 5, 7 and 9 dives): you stay on the islands, and accommodation, which is not included, is booked directly with the hotel.
- Private services and closed groups are available, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). A member of our team prepares the quote and coordinates an available instructor for the date.
- Through DIVE TO HEAL, more than 360 people with disabilities have been served. Accepted conditions include: hearing impairment (deaf), visual impairment (blind), reduced mobility (wheelchair), Down Syndrome, Cerebral Palsy, and Autism (depending on level and assessment). All instructors are trained in adaptive diving. Advance notice is recommended. The limitation is the presence of additional medical conditions that contraindicate diving.
- If you're already on the Rosario Islands and your hotel has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge.
- We dive in the Rosario Islands, inside the Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo National Natural Park, about 45-60 minutes by boat from Cartagena.
- All daytime activities (dive trips, mini-course, snorkeling, courses and each day of the packages) end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., followed by lunch. Guests departing from Cartagena have lunch included on the islands and the boat returns to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.); guests staying on the islands return to their hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m. for lunch (lunch not included). On overnight courses and packages, day 1's daytime activities also end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., and then you go to your hotel on the islands. Night diving (on plans that include it) is separate, in the evening (see each plan's schedule).
- There is always availability (confirmed by the business). We only close on December 25 and January 1, and a trip can be suspended due to adverse weather. The date and number of people are chosen in the booking link. To book for the next day, you need to do it before 4:30 p.m. (see booking system cutoff). Booking for the SAME day is no longer possible (trips leave in the morning and the website closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before): you book for the next available day.
- Each person can bring one backpack or bag on the boat. If the guest needs to bring a suitcase, it has to be arranged with a member of our team. If they prefer not to take it, we can store the suitcase at our office in Cartagena.
- What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.
- At our base on the island there are lockers where you can leave your things (clothes, phone, wallet) while you dive or snorkel.
- There is no minimum number of people: every activity runs even for a single person.
- Activities and courses are taught in Spanish and English. If a participant speaks neither language, they can come with someone who interprets for them, but instruction is still given in Spanish or English.
- Bookings are made on our website, through each activity's link (with the 10% online discount). The system closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you still book on the website, for the next available day. Plans with no booking link (the 3- and 4-dive packages, the 9-dive package from the islands, the 1-dive trip from the islands, Bubble Makers, Divemaster and the private service) are booked by an advisor in this chat.
- Besides the insurance form, each diver fills in a liability waiver. Our team sends it to you to complete (certified divers: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish)), and the confirmation email reminds you if you have not done it yet.
- The mini-course is a one-day try-dive, an introduction to diving: it does not certify, does not count as part of any PADI course and requires nothing from PADI beforehand (no PADI account or PADI online course). It is the same departing from Cartagena or already on the islands: there is no online or emailed theory; the theory is done there, on the day, along with pool practice and 1 ocean dive with an instructor.
- International clients pay 100% by card on the website; with a foreign card the passport is used as the ID document.
- Colombians and residents of Colombia (including holders of a cédula de extranjería) pay in pesos and do not use the website booking link: a team advisor always closes the booking in this chat and sends them the link, QR code or Llave to pay 100% online or a 50% deposit, and the other 50% on the day of the activity, by card or cash. The 50% deposit option is only for them. Nobody pays 100% at the dock without booking online.
- If you leave the next day around noon: from the Rosario Islands it is very tight (pickup is between 9:30 and 9:45 and the activity ends around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), so it is best to confirm it with a team advisor; departing from Cartagena it does not fit (the boat returns at 3:00 p.m. and arrives around 4:15 p.m.). To book for the next day you must do it before 4:30 p.m. the day before.
- Customers paying in US dollars book and pay through the online link: the payment is recorded right away and the team reconciles it shortly after to confirm the booking; only if the online payment fails does the team send a link to pay by transfer.
- If the booking system or the online payment fails, our team sends you a link to pay by bank transfer, and the 10% online discount is kept (because the online payment failed). Outside that case there is no payment by transfer: the 10% discount is for booking and paying online.
- In groups combining diving and snorkeling, snorkeling takes place in a different area from the dive sites. If there are few people everyone goes on the same boat; otherwise the group is split by activity.
- Besides our base (Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso, on Isla Grande), other hotels in the area with maritime access are Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao. Accommodation is not included: it is booked directly with the hotel.
- To book an activity departing from the islands, the customer must already have their hotel and tell us which one: pickup is arranged there. If they don't have it yet, they first book the hotel and message us with its name; then we book. If they booked the activity first, the hotel could be cancelled, it could be full, they could forget to tell us or end up departing from Cartagena. If they stay in a house, an Airbnb or a hotel not on our list, they tell us the name and an advisor confirms the pickup before they book and pay: they do not book until then.
- Returning to Cartagena on a different date from the plan is not included. If the guest wants to stay longer on the islands and come back with us another day, a member of our team arranges it (space on the boat, etc.).
- Departure and pickup times are fixed: they cannot be moved earlier or later. If you need an adjustment, a team advisor reviews it.
- Cancellations due to bad weather are unlikely because the Rosario Islands are in sheltered waters. If the Port Authority (Capitanía de Puerto) closes departures to the islands, we first try to reschedule the activity so you don't lose your booking. If rescheduling is not possible, you get a 100% refund. See the terms and conditions: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Scuba diving is not possible during pregnancy: no mini-course, no dive trips and no courses (DAN and obstetricians advise against it for the whole pregnancy). Surface snorkeling is possible, with her doctor's approval. Whoever comes with her can dive as usual.
- If you get seasick on the boat (the ride to the islands is about 1 hour by speedboat): have a light breakfast before leaving and consider seasickness tablets. If you take any medication, ask your doctor whether you can dive with it.
- We do issue invoices (also to companies). An advisor from our team coordinates the invoice details with the customer.
- There is no maximum age for diving: an older person can dive with the same medical form as everyone else.
- We carry oxygen and a first-aid kit on board, with trained staff, and there is an emergency protocol.
- Groups are small and follow PADI safety standards for each activity.
- The boat is a regular speedboat with no bathroom. On the islands we use the facilities of the hotel where lunch is served: that is where you change, use the bathroom and shower.
- Diving Planet has no parking of its own; there are public car parks in the old town area, and the easiest way to reach the pier is by taxi.
- There is no gift card, but you can book in someone else's name; the date and details are arranged with an advisor.
- Smoking is not allowed on the boat.
- Pets are not allowed on the boat: we go to a National Natural Park.
- Babies and young children who are not yet old enough for any activity (snorkeling starts at 6) can ride the boat with their parents at any age, and they ride free.
- You can bring your own camera on the dives or snorkeling, at your own risk. Diving Planet does not rent cameras.

reply:

The price depends on where you’ll be starting from, so I’m leaving both options below. From Cartagena, the course includes round-trip boat transport, National Park entrance, dive insurance, equipment, lunch, and an eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL. If you’re already on the Rosario Islands, it includes dive insurance, equipment, a PADI professional, and hotel boat pick-up if your hotel has maritime access; transport from Cartagena and lunch aren’t included.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
*From Cartagena* — boat from Muelle de la Bodeguita · lunch included
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD
*Already on the Rosario Islands* — pickup at your hotel if it has boat access · no lunch
• Dive Mini Course: 134 USD · 149 USD

Keep in mind that the mini-course is a one-day introduction and does not certify you; to get certified there is the Open Water course (2 days, with a night on the islands).

Would you leave *from Cartagena* or are you already *on the Rosario Islands*? Then I'll give you the exact plan. 🌊

msg: Hi, my flight lands in Cartagena on Saturday at 11:30 am and I leave on Sunday at 8 pm. I'm PADI Advanced, last dive 3 months ago. Could I fit in some diving? I'm from the UK.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

You’d need to wait at least 18 hours after your last dive before flying. If you do a daytime dive on Saturday, you could fly from 7:00 a.m. Sunday, so your 8:00 p.m. flight meets that interval.

However, the Cartagena boat leaves at 8:00 a.m. and returns around 4:15 p.m., so you’d miss Saturday’s departure because you land at 11:30 a.m. The next day’s trip would be too late for your Sunday flight. Unfortunately, diving from Cartagena won’t fit this itinerary.

There is always availability: we operate every day, including public holidays, except December 25 and January 1; if sea conditions are not safe, the trip is rescheduled.

Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor to check whether there’s an option from the islands?

msg: Solo yo. ¿A qué hora me recogerían en el Cocoliso y tengo que llevar algo? Gracias.
reply:
En Cocoliso, la recogida es entre las 9:30 y las 9:45. Lleva tu carné de buceo, bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda; el equipo de buceo está incluido. También debes completar el formato del seguro que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.

También necesitas:
• Estar listo a las 9:30 en tu hotel
• Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente. El refresher es el minicurso (piscina y una inmersión con instructor) y ocupa su propio día: ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo. Quien viene varios días hace el refresher el primero y bucea los demás.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.

¿Han pasado *más de 2 años* desde tu última inmersión?

msg: Good afternoon. I am from Germany and I hold an Open Water certification, although I have not dived for three years. I am staying in Getsemaní and I would like to dive next Wednesday. My flight home leaves on Thursday at 22:00. Is this possible, and what would you recommend?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

You can fly from 7:00 a.m. on Thursday after a daytime refresher on Wednesday, so your 22:00 flight meets the 18-hour interval. The wait is counted from your last dive, not from your return to Cartagena.

Since you’re certified but haven’t dived for three years, I’d recommend a **Refresher**. It’s booked as the Dive Mini Course, but for certified divers the 18-hour flying rule applies. The activity ends around 12:00–1:00 p.m.; the boat returns to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m., arriving around 4:15 p.m.

You can choose Wednesday and the number of people in the booking calendar here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/minicurso-de-buceo/2?language=en. The website closes bookings for the next day at 4:30 p.m. the day before.

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

There is always availability: we operate every day, including public holidays, except December 25 and January 1; if sea conditions are not safe, the trip is rescheduled.

Would you like to book the refresher for Wednesday?

msg: Thank you. What exactly does the refresher consist of? I would prefer to do proper dives on Wednesday: could I do a short review with the guide in the morning and then the 2 dives on the same day? I could also come on Tuesday if necessary.
reply:
The refresher includes pool practice and one reef dive with a PADI instructor. It takes the full day, so the two-dive trip can’t be done on the same day. Since you haven’t dived for three years, a refresher is normally required; doing it Tuesday would let you do the two dives on Wednesday.

For the refresher, meet at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. The boat returns to Cartagena around 3:00 p.m., arriving at approximately 4:15 p.m. It includes the boat, equipment, lunch, dive insurance, National Park entrance fee, and an eco-social contribution to DIVE TO HEAL. Ground transport to the dock and underwater photos or videos aren’t included.

After your last dive, wait at least 18 hours before flying. A Wednesday daytime dive would allow you to fly from 7:00 a.m. Thursday, so your 10:00 p.m. flight fits that interval.

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

Question: What is the Rescue Diver course and why is it important?
Other ways to ask: What does the Rescue Diver course involve and what are its benefits? / Why is it relevant to take the Rescue Diver course?
Answer: Rescue Diver is an advanced recreational course focused on prevention, emergency management, and diver rescue. To take this course, you need to have Advanced Open Water certification and recent EFR or first-aid training. The course covers self-rescue techniques, stress recognition, panic management, missing diver search, rescue scenarios, and emergency response. It is more mentally demanding than physically demanding, and many divers consider it transformative because it shifts the diver's mindset toward safety, awareness, leadership, and prevention. It does not grant a professional level; the first professional level is Divemaster.

This package is available both for departures from Cartagena and for those already on the islands. msg: Good, thank you. Two last questions: do you pick me up in Getsemaní or how do I reach the dock, and do I have to bring my certification card or fill in any forms for these two days?
reply:
There’s no hotel pick-up in Getsemaní. Please make your own way to **Muelle de la Bodeguita** for the **8:00 a.m.** departure; ground transportation to the dock isn’t included. Ask for **DIVING PLANET at entrance 3**. [Map](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Muelle+de+la+Bodeguita/@10.4199447,-75.5537609,828m/data=!3m2!1e3!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x8ef62f753729822d:0x1bbcdd8224d0eaaf!8m2!3d10.4199447!4d-75.551186!16s%2Fg%2F113gzkckf?entry=ttu)

Please bring your **Open Water certification card**; you can show it on the day or send a photo beforehand. You’ll need to complete:
- The **course medical form** for the refresher: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol

- The **certified-diver liability waiver** for your Wednesday dives: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol

The forms are in Spanish. There’s no theory to complete beforehand; the refresher review is done with the instructor on the day.

• If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
• After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying
• Minimum age: 10 and over.
• For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
• What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.

reply:
¡Hola! 🪸 Soy *Coral*, de *Diving Planet* — buceamos todo el año en las Islas del Rosario, saliendo desde Cartagena o desde las propias islas. 🌊

¡Qué buen plan para disfrutar dos días de buceo en las Islas del Rosario! Para dos días, desde Cartagena tienen estas opciones:

- **4 inmersiones diurnas:** 351 USD / 1.282.000 COP por persona a precio normal; 316 USD / 1.154.000 COP online.
- **5 inmersiones, incluida una nocturna:** 436 USD / 1.587.000 COP por persona a precio normal; 392 USD / 1.429.000 COP online.

Por ser 6, aplica **10% de descuento para grupos de 5 o más**, que se suma al 10% online. Deben solicitarlo al equipo **antes de pagar**; no se aplica automáticamente. El descuento de grupo no aplica a cursos PADI.

Quienes lleven el equipo completo pueden acceder al **5% por equipo propio**, pero ese descuento **no se suma al de grupo**: cada uno se combina solo con el descuento online. El equipo debe incluir regulador, BCD/chaleco, traje, máscara y aletas.

No hay descuento ni tarifa especial por ser colombiano: el precio es el mismo, solo cambia la moneda (COP).

Para aplicar el descuento de grupo y cerrar la reserva, ¿quieres que te pase con un asesor del equipo?

msg: Hey! I'm an American diver, Advanced Open Water. I'm renting a house on Airbnb on Isla Grande next week, it's called Villa Marea. I'd like to do two dives. Can you pick me up there? How does that work?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Great that you're staying on Isla Grande — the diving around the Rosario Islands is beautiful, and two dives is a perfect way to enjoy it. 🐠

Since you're staying in a house (an Airbnb) and not at one of the hotels on our list, here's how it works: you tell us the name of the house, and a team advisor confirms the pick-up logistics **before** you book and pay. So we don't book until that's confirmed.

A few things to keep in mind:
- Pick-up is coordinated from places with maritime access. In some cases the boat arrives directly; in others we'll point you to the nearest dock or meeting point, or a short walk to our dive center.
- If your place has boat access, pick-up and drop-off by boat are included at no extra charge.
- The pick-up point and exact time are confirmed by a team advisor.

For the two dives, the plan is **Fun Dives – 2 dives (1 day, already on the islands)**:
- 124 USD / 440.000 COP online (138 USD / 489.000 COP regular)
- Certification required (you're Advanced Open Water, so you're all set)
- Gear included, lunch not included
- Typical schedule: hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m., 2 open-water dives with a surface interval at the base, and back around 12:00–1:00 p.m.

Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor so they can confirm the pick-up at Villa Marea before you book?

msg: Gracias. Nos interesa el minicurso, para los dos. ¿A qué profundidad se baja? Y mi esposa pregunta si hace falta saber nadar muy bien, porque ella nada lo justo. Quisiéramos ir el sábado 14 de noviembre.
reply:
El minicurso llega hasta 12 metros; lo habitual es bucear entre 5 y 12, según el punto elegido. No hace falta experiencia previa, pero no tengo a la mano el requisito específico sobre qué tan bien hay que nadar. Como ella nada lo justo, es mejor confirmarlo con el equipo antes de reservar.

También necesitas:
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 12 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

El vuelo del domingo por la noche no sería compatible: después de la última inmersión debes esperar al menos 18 horas antes de volar. El regreso a Cartagena no cambia ese tiempo.

Para el Curso Open Water, sí: debes completar antes la teoría en PADI eLearning, que toma aproximadamente 10 a 12 horas. El curso también requiere alojarte al menos una noche en las islas; el alojamiento no está incluido. El asesor ya tiene tu caso sobre el asma y te escribirá por aquí.

msg: Good call on asking: one of the certified guys, Mike, last dived about three years ago. The other two dived last summer. No beers, got it. So what does Mike need to do? And who do I talk to on your team to get the group discount before we pay?
reply:
Mike is still a certified diver, but since it’s been about three years, a refresher is normally required. It’s a pool session and one dive with an instructor, and it takes a separate day—he can’t do the refresher and the dive trip on the same day. If he has already completed a refresher or PADI ReActivate at another center, that counts. Very experienced divers with 500+ dives or Dive Master level can be reviewed by a team advisor.

To request the group discount, contact the team **before paying**. The 10% group discount applies to recreational diving and mini-courses, and stacks with the 10% online discount. It isn’t applied automatically and can’t be added after payment. Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor?

You'll also need:
• There is no theory to do beforehand: it is done there, on the day, with the instructor.
• The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
• To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
• After diving, wait at least 18 hours before flying
• Minimum age: 10 and over.
• What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.

rag.answer:
Mike is still a certified diver, but since it’s been about three years, a refresher is normally required. If he has already completed a refresher or PADI ReActivate at another center, that counts. Very experienced divers with 500+ dives or Dive Master level can be reviewed by a team advisor.

To request the group discount, contact the team **before paying**. The 10% group discount applies to recreational diving and mini-courses, and stacks with the 10% online discount. It isn’t applied automatically and can’t be added after payment. Would you like me to connect you with a team advisor?

The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. • To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.

Question: How long do I have to wait to fly after diving?
Other ways to ask: Can I fly the same day I dive? / What's the minimum time between diving and flying?
Answer: Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). The refresher is also 18 hours: it is for certified divers, even though it is booked as the mini course. The hours count from the last dive, not from the return to Cartagena. The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.

Question: Is diving safe?
Other ways to ask: Is it safe to go diving? / Are there risks in diving or is it considered safe?
Answer: Yes, diving is safe when procedures and training limits are followed. The basic rules are: never hold your breath, ascend slowly, always dive with a buddy, equalize early and often, respect depth limits, constantly monitor your air, and follow the instructor or guide. The bot can give general guidance, but it cannot clear someone medically or replace a dive professional's judgment.

[10] Fuente: faqs
Question: Are fish, sharks, starfish, coral, or sea urchins dangerous?
Other ways to ask: Is it dangerous to encounter sharks, fish, or sea urchins while diving? / Should I be concerned about marine animals like coral or starfish when diving?
Answer: Most fish avoid humans. If you see a shark, the recommended approach is to stay calm, observe, and enjoy the moment from a respectful distance; encounters are usually safe. Touching starfish, turtles, coral, or any organism is not recommended: many are delicate or sensitive. Many minor diving injuries occur from accidental contact with coral or sea urchins, which is why neutral buoyancy and not touching anything are fundamental for safety.

msg: Hiya! I'm Priya, a British backpacker on a tight budget, currently in Santa Marta and heading to Cartagena next week. I've got a hostel in Getsemaní booked already.
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Hiya, Priya! Getting your first certification is a fantastic goal, and the Open Water course can fit within your three free days: the course itself takes two days. You’d need to arrange accommodation on the Rosario Islands for the night between course days; your Getsemaní hostel wouldn’t cover that overnight stay.

The course includes online theory, pool sessions and four certification dives. From Cartagena, it starts at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. on day one and returns around 4:15 p.m. on day two. I’m leaving the course prices below.

• PADI Basic Course (Open Water): 693 USD · 770 USD

- Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.

- Colombians (anyone with Colombian nationality, holding a Colombian cédula or passport, wherever they live; also dual nationals when one nationality is Colombian) and residents of Colombia (holders of a cédula de extranjería, a resident ID; living in Colombia without one is not enough) pay in Colombian pesos (COP). msg: Me alojo en el centro histórico. ¿A qué hora y dónde hay que estar, y qué incluye el precio?
reply:
El encuentro es a las 8:00 a. m. en el Muelle de la Bodeguita, a 5 minutos del centro histórico. No hay recogida en el hotel; cada persona llega por su cuenta al muelle y el transporte terrestre no está incluido. El regreso a Cartagena es a las 3:00 p. m., con llegada estimada a las 4:15 p. m.

El refresher incluye la entrada al Parque Nacional Natural, seguro obligatorio de buceo, lancha Cartagena-Islas-Cartagena, entrenamiento en piscina y una inmersión en el mar con instructor PADI, equipo de buceo, almuerzo y aporte eco-social a DIVE TO HEAL. No incluye transporte terrestre al muelle, fotos o videos submarinos, propinas voluntarias, comida adicional ni regreso en una fecha distinta a la programada.

También incluye:
• 2 inmersiones guiadas con un profesional PADI certificado

El *refresher* es un repaso con instructor antes de volver a bucear: se reserva como *Minicurso de Buceo* y cuesta *655.000 COP* por persona que lo necesite. Lleva el formulario médico de curso (aunque estén certificados, el enlace llega con la reserva). ¿Te interesa?

- **Tu hijo de 11 años:** puede hacer el minicurso de buceo, que no requiere certificación previa. También puede hacer snorkel.

Se pueden combinar actividades en un mismo tour, aunque el grupo puede dividirse por actividad según la operación.

msg: Hi, I'm a German traveler in Cartagena and I've never dived. I'd like to get my Open Water certification. How long does the course take?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

The Open Water course takes **2 days** and certifies you to dive down to **18 m**. It’s a great way to start diving! 🌊

From Cartagena, you meet at **Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. on Day 1**. The course includes online PADI theory before the trip, pool practice, and four certification dives across the two days. You’ll need to stay overnight on the islands after Day 1; accommodation isn’t included and is booked directly with the hotel. You return to Cartagena on Day 2 at **3:00 p.m.** (estimated arrival around **4:15 p.m.**).

The online price is **USD 693 per person**; the regular price is **USD 770 per person**. Would you like the booking link?

msg: ¿Ella puede hacer algo en el agua? ¿Y necesitaría algún permiso médico?
reply:
Sí, puede hacer snorkel en superficie, con el visto bueno de su médico. Durante el embarazo no se recomienda bucear con botella.

Para el snorkel, la edad mínima es de 6 años. Debe llegar puntual al punto de encuentro a las 8:00 a. m. y completar el formato para procesar el seguro, que se envía en el correo de confirmación. Que consulte con su médico antes de entrar al agua; no puedo determinar qué autorización médica necesita en su caso.

También necesitas:
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

¿Te animas con la *salida de 2 inmersiones*, un *paquete de varios días* o un *curso avanzado*? 🌊

The Rosario Islands are a beautiful place to enjoy several dives, and we have multi-day packages for certified divers.

Online bookings receive the 10% online discount. Accommodation isn’t included, and the multi-day packages include lunch on day one only. Since your last dive was 10 years ago, a refresher is normally required before diving; it takes a separate day. If you’ve already completed a refresher or PADI ReActivate elsewhere, that counts.

• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 316 USD · 351 USD
• 5 Dives - 2 days: 392 USD · 436 USD

• 9 Dives - 4 days: 602 USD · 668 USD
*Already on the Rosario Islands* — pickup at your hotel if it has boat access · no lunch

msg: Tell me about the 3-dive package with a night dive. Where would I sleep and is the hotel included?
reply:
Great choice — the night dive is a really special experience, the reef comes alive in a completely different way after dark. 🌙

Here's how the 3-dive package works (2 daytime dives + 1 night dive, all in one day):

- Meeting at Muelle de la Bodeguita at 8:00 a.m. + speedboat transfer (about 1 hour)
- Arrival at our island base, equipment setup
- 2 dives + surface interval + lunch (included)
- 1 night dive
- After the activity you stay overnight on the islands, and the next day you return to Cartagena on our boat (leaves the base at 3:00 p.m., arrives around 4:15 p.m.)

About where you sleep: the hotel is *not included*. Because the package has a night dive, you must stay one night on the Rosario Islands, and you book your accommodation directly with the hotel. Our base is at Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso on Isla Grande — if you stay at either, pick-up is direct. Other hotels in the area with maritime access are Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao.

It includes the National Park entrance fee, dive insurance, boat transport Cartagena–Islands–Cartagena, 3 guided dives with a PADI professional, diving equipment and lunch on day 1.

One thing to keep in mind: since it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required, and it takes its own day — the dive trip can't be done the same day.

*From Cartagena* — boat from Muelle de la Bodeguita · lunch included (on multi-day plans, the first day's)

• 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive): 287 USD · 319 USD
• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 316 USD · 351 USD
*Already on the Rosario Islands* — pickup at your hotel if it has boat access · no lunch
• Fun Dives - 2 dives (1 day): 124 USD · 138 USD
• 3-dive package (1 day, 2 daytime + 1 night dive): 188 USD · 209 USD
• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 204 USD · 227 USD

msg: Do I need a refresher since it's been so long? And how do I book?
reply:
Since it’s been 10 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required. It’s a one-day mini course with pool practice and one reef dive with an instructor, so it can’t be done on the same day as your 2-dive trip. If you’ve already completed a refresher or PADI ReActivate at another dive center, that counts. With about 30 dives, the experienced-diver review exception (500+ dives or Dive Master) wouldn’t apply.

The 10% online discount is applied automatically. The booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before; after that, you can still book online for the next available day. Please bring your certification card, and complete the required medical form for the refresher: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol

*Prices per person* (online · regular):
• 4-dive package (2 days, 4 daytime dives): 316 USD · 351 USD
• Dive Mini Course: 183 USD · 204 USD

Guests who are not Colombian or residents of Colombia pay in US dollars (USD) by card on the website; the rate is the same, only the currency changes.

How many people would this be for: just you, or more? 😊

msg: Un detalle: mi esposo buceó por última vez en abril de 2022 y yo en enero de este año, en Capurganá. ¿Eso cambia algo para él?
reply:
Sí, para tu esposo cambia: como su última inmersión fue en abril de 2022, normalmente necesitaría hacer un refresher antes de volver a bucear. El refresher es un minicurso con práctica en piscina y una inmersión con instructor, y ocupa un día; como vienen varios días, podría hacerlo el primer día y bucear los demás. Si ya hizo un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, eso cuenta y puede bucear directamente. Para ti, con una inmersión en enero de este año, no aplica ese requisito por tiempo sin bucear.

También necesitas:
• No hay teoría que hacer antes: se hace allí, el mismo día, con el instructor.
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Si llevas más de 2 años sin bucear, normalmente se requiere un refresh; los buzos muy experimentados (500+ inmersiones, Dive Master) los revisa un asesor del equipo. Si ya hiciste un refresh o un PADI ReActivate en otro centro, cuenta como tu refresh y puedes bucear directamente. El refresher es el minicurso (piscina y una inmersión con instructor) y ocupa su propio día: ese mismo día no se hace la salida de buceo. Quien viene varios días hace el refresher el primero y bucea los demás.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.
• Ser buzo certificado y presentar tu carnet

El *refresher* es un repaso con instructor antes de volver a bucear: se reserva como *Minicurso de Buceo* y cuesta *655.000 COP* por persona que lo necesite. Lleva el formulario médico de curso (aunque estén certificados, el enlace llega con la reserva). ¿Les interesa?

msg: ¿Qué incluye cada salida? Queremos saber si hay que llevar almuerzo y si el transporte hasta el muelle corre por nuestra cuenta.
reply:
Para el buceo certificado, cada salida incluye la entrada al Parque Nacional, seguro obligatorio, lancha rápida Cartagena–Islas–Cartagena, dos inmersiones guiadas con un profesional PADI, equipo de buceo, almuerzo y aporte eco-social a DIVE TO HEAL. No necesitan llevar almuerzo; si requieren comida adicional, esa sí corre por cuenta de ustedes.

El transporte terrestre hasta el muelle no está incluido: cada persona llega por su cuenta al Muelle de la Bodeguita, a las 8:00 a. m. El regreso a Cartagena es a las 3:00 p. m., con llegada estimada a las 4:15 p. m.

El *refresher* es un repaso con instructor antes de volver a bucear: se reserva como *Minicurso de Buceo* y cuesta *655.000 COP* por persona que lo necesite. Lleva el formulario médico de curso (aunque estén certificados, el enlace llega con la reserva). ¿Les interesa?

msg: My husband is a certified Advanced diver (his last dive was in Cozumel this past March). Our daughter is 11 and has never tried scuba, and our son is 6. I don't dive. What could each of us do?
reply:
That sounds like a lovely family plan! Since you’ll be staying at Cocoliso, pickup there is included.

- Your husband can join certified dives; with Advanced certification, his maximum depth is 30 m.
- Your 11-year-old can try the Dive Mini Course, which is available from age 10.
- Your 6-year-old can join snorkeling, available from age 6.
- You can join the snorkeling tour too, or enjoy the boat as a non-diving companion.

Minors must be accompanied by a parent or responsible relative. 🌊

Which one are you leaning toward — *diving*, a *mini-course*, *snorkeling* or a *PADI course*? 🌊

msg: Great, thanks. So the plan would be: my husband diving, our 11-year-old trying scuba for the first time, and me and our 6-year-old snorkeling, all on December 3 from Hotel Cocoliso. We're US citizens. How do we book and pay?
reply:
Perfect! Your plan works: your husband can join certified diving, your 11-year-old can try the Dive Mini Course, and you and your 6-year-old can snorkel. At 6, snorkeling is the available in-water activity. Pickup at Hotel Cocoliso is included.

For your 11-year-old’s mini-course, book and pay online here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/dive-mini-course-already-on-island/20?language=en. The online booking includes a 10% discount. As international guests, you pay in USD by card; payment is recorded right away, then the team reconciles it shortly after to confirm the booking. If online payment fails, the team can provide a bank-transfer payment link.

The snorkeling booking is here: https://book.divingplanet.org/book/snorkeling-already-on-the-island/25?language=en. Certified diving is booked through a team advisor. The booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before, so for December 3, please book before that cutoff. Minors must be accompanied by a responsible adult.

There is always availability: we operate every day, including public holidays, except December 25 and January 1; if sea conditions are not safe, the trip is rescheduled.

For the one who hasn't chosen yet I'd recommend these options. Which one do they like best? 🐠
• *Certified diving* — Guided dives for already-certified divers; explore the reef at depth.
• *Dive mini-course* — A first time underwater with an instructor: pool training and a real dive. No experience needed.
• *Open Water course* — Entry certification course: qualifies you to dive independently down to 18 m.
• *Snorkeling* — Enjoy the reef from the surface, with mask and fins. Great for families.
• *Come along as a companion* — Comes on the boat and enjoys the day with the group, without getting in the water.

msg: Hello! My partner and I are from Dublin and we're staying in an Airbnb on Isla Grande from November 15 to 19. Could you pick us up there for a morning in the water?
reply:
Hi! 🪸 I'm *Coral* from *Diving Planet* — we dive year-round in the Rosario Islands, departing from Cartagena or right from the islands. 🌊

Great that you'll be staying on Isla Grande — the Rosario Islands are a beautiful spot for a morning in the water. 🌊

Yes, if you're already on the islands and your accommodation has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge. In some cases the boat comes directly to the hotel; in others we'll point you to the nearest dock or meeting point. The exact pick-up point and time are coordinated by a team advisor, who'll also ask for the name of your Airbnb.

A couple of things to keep in mind:
- From the islands, hotel pick-up is between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (8:00 a.m. for specialties), and daytime activities end around 12:00–1:00 p.m.
- Pick-up times are fixed and can't be moved earlier or later.

To point you to the right plan, could you tell me a bit more about what you'd like to do — snorkeling, a first-time dive experience, or fun dives (for certified divers)? And is it just the two of you?

Once I know that, I'll share the options and prices so we can get your booking started. 😊

msg: A health question: my partner had asthma as a child and used an inhaler, but hasn't needed it in more than ten years. Is that a problem for the mini course? Is there a form to fill in?

• Be ready at 9:30 a.m. at your hotel
• To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
• After diving, wait at least 12 hours before flying
• Minimum age: 10 and over.
• What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.

For specific medical questions, it's important that you speak with our qualified staff so they can assess your particular situation. I'm passing you now to someone from our team, who will write to you here shortly.

msg: ¿Los niños pueden bucear con esas edades? Al de 9 le encanta el mar, pero no sé si es muy chico para el minicurso.
reply:
¡Qué lindo que le encante el mar! Con 9 años todavía es muy chico para el minicurso, que es desde los 10. Pero puede hacer *Bubble Makers*, una experiencia introductoria en piscina o aguas muy poco profundas (máximo 2 m), con un instructor dedicado, o disfrutar del *snorkel*, disponible desde los 6 años.

Con 13 años puede hacer snorkel, el minicurso o el curso Open Water; también puede tomar Advanced o Rescue, desde los 12. Los menores deben estar acompañados por un adulto responsable.

Si quieres, te ayudo a reservar: *Minicurso de buceo*. ¿Te animas? 🌊

msg: ¿Cómo es el curso Open Water con ustedes? ¿Cuántos días dura, hay que estudiar algo antes y se puede ir y volver a Cartagena cada día?
reply:
¡Qué chévere que quieran certificarse! El Open Water es el curso inicial completo: incluye teoría, práctica en piscina y 4 inmersiones en aguas abiertas. Dura **2 días** y la certificación permite bucear con otro buzo certificado hasta **18 metros**.

Antes de empezar la parte práctica, deben completar la teoría en **PADI eLearning**, que toma aproximadamente **10 a 12 horas**.

No se puede ir y volver a Cartagena cada día: el primer día se quedan en las islas y necesitan alojarse allí **al menos una noche**. El alojamiento no está incluido y se reserva directamente con el hotel.

Desde Cartagena, el primer día salen a las **8:00 a. m.** desde el Muelle de la Bodeguita. Hacen piscina y dos inmersiones; el segundo día completan la piscina y las dos inmersiones restantes, y regresan a Cartagena a las **3:00 p. m.** (llegada aproximada a las 4:15 p. m.). El almuerzo está incluido el primer día, pero no el segundo.

También necesitas:
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.

¿Saldrías *desde Cartagena* o ya estás *en las Islas del Rosario*? Así te paso el plan exacto. 🌊

Diving Planet policies:
- Wait at least 18 hours to take a flight after recreational diving. 12 hours minimum after the mini course (only for non-certified divers). The refresher is also 18 hours: it is for certified divers, even though it is booked as the mini course. The hours count from the last dive, not from the return to Cartagena. The mini course dive ends around 12:00 (noon): its 12 hours count from then. If the last dive is a daytime one, the refresher's included (activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), you can fly from 7:00 a.m. the next day; after the mini-course, from midnight that same day. If the last dive is a night dive, the hours count from it. A flight the next day at 7:00 a.m. or later IS fine: they can dive the day before, and that day's return time to Cartagena changes nothing. For a certified diver, a flight on the SAME day as the dive NEVER works, whatever the time, even at night: with a flight on Sunday night, the last dive must be on Saturday at the latest; the boat being back before they leave does not fix it. If they say they leave that day without saying how, they are probably flying: tell them this. When answering, first say from what time they can fly and then compare it with their flight; do not start with yes or no.
- If it's been more than 2 years since your last dive, a refresher is normally required; very experienced divers (500+ dives, Dive Master) are reviewed by a member of our team. If you already did a refresher or a PADI ReActivate at another centre, it counts as your refresher and you can dive directly. The refresher is the mini course (pool and one dive with an instructor) and takes its own day: the dive trip cannot be done that same day. Anyone staying several days does the refresher on the first day and dives on the others.
- For recreational dive outings, the refresher and the courses for already-certified divers (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster and specialties), you must present your certified diver card. You can send us a photo of it beforehand or show it on the day of the activity.
- Muelle de la Bodeguita, 5 minutes from the historic center, at 8:00 AM. Departing from Cartagena there is no hotel pick-up: each person gets to the dock on their own (ground transportation to the dock is not included).
- By booking you accept our terms and conditions, cancellation policy, and data treatment. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Date changes are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Changes to the number of people on a booking you already made are subject to availability and our terms and conditions. See: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Colombians (anyone with Colombian nationality, holding a Colombian cédula or passport, wherever they live; also dual nationals when one nationality is Colombian) and residents of Colombia (holders of a cédula de extranjería, a resident ID; living in Colombia without one is not enough) pay in Colombian pesos (COP). Saying they are Colombian or from a Colombian city ("I'm from Cali") already says it; what is not enough is only having been born there while living abroad: then ask whether they hold Colombian nationality or a cédula de extranjería. All other international clients pay in US dollars (USD). A group does not pay in parts: if the same booking mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group pays in US dollars (USD), residents and Colombians included. A Colombian together with someone who holds a cédula de extranjería, wherever they are from, is not a mixed group: both pay in pesos (COP). The price is the same: only the currency changes (there is no discount for being Colombian).
- If the group mixes Colombians or residents with international clients who hold no cédula de extranjería, the whole group booking is paid in US dollars (USD), at the same equivalent price. Someone with a cédula de extranjería does not count as a foreigner, wherever they are from. There is no different price for being Colombian.
- If you are already on the Rosario Islands, we coordinate pick-up and drop-off from hotels with maritime access. In some cases the boat arrives directly at the hotel; in others we indicate the nearest dock or meeting point.
- These plans have different prices because they do not include transport from Cartagena or lunch.
- Pick-up is only on the Rosario Islands: Barú (including Playa Blanca, which is on Barú) is not part of the islands and we do not operate or pick up there; guests staying in Barú depart from Cartagena (Muelle de la Bodeguita).
- It depends on the activity: snorkeling from 6 years old; Bubble Makers from 8 to 10 years old (pool mini-course and very shallow water practice, max 2 meters); the dive mini-course and the Open Water course from 10 years old; the Advanced course and the Rescue course from 12. Minors must be accompanied by a demonstrable parent or responsible relative.
- The medical form is required for courses or mini-courses: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). The link can be sent together with the booking link; if you have not completed it, it is sent again in the booking confirmation email. Exception: the refresher (a review with an instructor) uses the course medical form, even if you are a certified diver.
- If you are a certified diver, there are no additional medical restrictions; your liability waiver is the certified-diver one: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish). For the refresher day this one is not used: use the course medical form.
- Bringing or drinking alcohol on the boat or during the activity is not allowed, and no alcohol or other substances may be consumed before diving. You must be in good physical condition.
- The booking system on our website. It automatically closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you can no longer book for the next day, and you still book on the website for the next available day.
- To process the insurance, you must complete the form we send in the booking confirmation email.
- From Cartagena: departure at 8:00 a.m. from Muelle de la Bodeguita and return at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.). From the islands: hotel pick-up between 9:30 and 9:45 a.m. (8:00 a.m. for specialties and 7:30 a.m. on day 2 of some courses). Daytime activities end around 12:00-1:00 p.m. (see the activity schedule). Night diving: in the evening (pick-up around 5:30 p.m., back around 7:30 p.m.). Online booking system closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before; after that, you book on the website for the next available day.
- We only close on December 25 and January 1. The rest of the year we operate every day, including public holidays, except for suspension due to adverse weather conditions.
- The tour includes water all day, coconut candy between dives, and lunch (rice with chicken or rice with vegetables). The menu is always the same, it does not change by day/supplier. Vegetarians, vegans, and celiacs receive rice with vegetables. Guests may bring their own food if needed (e.g. allergy or special diet). If the guest has a food allergy, they must inform us before the tour. In multi-day packages departing from Cartagena, lunch is included on the first day only; plans for guests already on the islands do not include lunch.
- Photos and videos are not offered proactively or included in the price. The instructor may take them voluntarily and delivers them by the next day at the latest. Any tip to the instructor for photos/videos is voluntary: each guest gives whatever they like, directly to them. This applies to every activity, including the mini-course (and the refresher, booked as a mini-course), PADI courses and certified-diver trips: not included, the instructor may take them voluntarily.
- The 3, 4, 5, 7 and 9 dive packages are exclusively for certified divers with a minimum Open Water level. They are not available for uncertified beginners.
- Two-day courses (Open Water, Referral Course, Advanced, Rescue and Mindful Diving) require accommodation on the islands: at least one night, the night of day 1 (there is no return to Cartagena on day 1). There is no option to commute from Cartagena on both days. Accommodation is not included and must be booked directly with the hotel. The same goes for multi-day dive packages (4, 5, 7 and 9 dives): you stay on the islands, and accommodation, which is not included, is booked directly with the hotel.
- Private services and closed groups are available, with no fixed price (it depends on the group and the date). A member of our team prepares the quote and coordinates an available instructor for the date.
- Through DIVE TO HEAL, more than 360 people with disabilities have been served. Accepted conditions include: hearing impairment (deaf), visual impairment (blind), reduced mobility (wheelchair), Down Syndrome, Cerebral Palsy, and Autism (depending on level and assessment). All instructors are trained in adaptive diving. Advance notice is recommended. The limitation is the presence of additional medical conditions that contraindicate diving.
- If you're already on the Rosario Islands and your hotel has maritime access, boat pick-up and drop-off are included at no extra charge.
- We dive in the Rosario Islands, inside the Corales del Rosario y San Bernardo National Natural Park, about 45-60 minutes by boat from Cartagena.
- All daytime activities (dive trips, mini-course, snorkeling, courses and each day of the packages) end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., followed by lunch. Guests departing from Cartagena have lunch included on the islands and the boat returns to Cartagena at 3:00 p.m. (arriving around 4:15 p.m.); guests staying on the islands return to their hotel around 12:00-1:00 p.m. for lunch (lunch not included). On overnight courses and packages, day 1's daytime activities also end around 12:00-1:00 p.m., and then you go to your hotel on the islands. Night diving (on plans that include it) is separate, in the evening (see each plan's schedule).
- There is always availability (confirmed by the business). We only close on December 25 and January 1, and a trip can be suspended due to adverse weather. The date and number of people are chosen in the booking link. To book for the next day, you need to do it before 4:30 p.m. (see booking system cutoff). Booking for the SAME day is no longer possible (trips leave in the morning and the website closes at 4:30 p.m. the day before): you book for the next available day.
- Each person can bring one backpack or bag on the boat. If the guest needs to bring a suitcase, it has to be arranged with a member of our team. If they prefer not to take it, we can store the suitcase at our office in Cartagena.
- What to bring: swimsuit, towel, sunscreen, sunglasses and comfortable clothes. Diving or snorkeling gear is included in dive trips, the mini-course, snorkeling and PADI courses; the Divemaster uses their own gear.
- At our base on the island there are lockers where you can leave your things (clothes, phone, wallet) while you dive or snorkel.
- There is no minimum number of people: every activity runs even for a single person.
- Activities and courses are taught in Spanish and English. If a participant speaks neither language, they can come with someone who interprets for them, but instruction is still given in Spanish or English.
- Bookings are made on our website, through each activity's link (with the 10% online discount). The system closes at 4:30 PM the day before: after that time you still book on the website, for the next available day. Plans with no booking link (the 3- and 4-dive packages, the 9-dive package from the islands, the 1-dive trip from the islands, Bubble Makers, Divemaster and the private service) are booked by an advisor in this chat.
- Besides the insurance form, each diver fills in a liability waiver. Our team sends it to you to complete (certified divers: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-buzo-en-espanol (the form is in Spanish)), and the confirmation email reminds you if you have not done it yet.
- The mini-course is a one-day try-dive, an introduction to diving: it does not certify, does not count as part of any PADI course and requires nothing from PADI beforehand (no PADI account or PADI online course). It is the same departing from Cartagena or already on the islands: there is no online or emailed theory; the theory is done there, on the day, along with pool practice and 1 ocean dive with an instructor.
- International clients pay 100% by card on the website; with a foreign card the passport is used as the ID document.
- Colombians and residents of Colombia (including holders of a cédula de extranjería) pay in pesos and do not use the website booking link: a team advisor always closes the booking in this chat and sends them the link, QR code or Llave to pay 100% online or a 50% deposit, and the other 50% on the day of the activity, by card or cash. The 50% deposit option is only for them. Nobody pays 100% at the dock without booking online.
- If you leave the next day around noon: from the Rosario Islands it is very tight (pickup is between 9:30 and 9:45 and the activity ends around 12:00-1:00 p.m.), so it is best to confirm it with a team advisor; departing from Cartagena it does not fit (the boat returns at 3:00 p.m. and arrives around 4:15 p.m.). To book for the next day you must do it before 4:30 p.m. the day before.
- Customers paying in US dollars book and pay through the online link: the payment is recorded right away and the team reconciles it shortly after to confirm the booking; only if the online payment fails does the team send a link to pay by transfer.
- If the booking system or the online payment fails, our team sends you a link to pay by bank transfer, and the 10% online discount is kept (because the online payment failed). Outside that case there is no payment by transfer: the 10% discount is for booking and paying online.
- In groups combining diving and snorkeling, snorkeling takes place in a different area from the dive sites. If there are few people everyone goes on the same boat; otherwise the group is split by activity.
- Besides our base (Hotel San Pedro de Majagua and Hotel Cocoliso, on Isla Grande), other hotels in the area with maritime access are Rosario de Mar, Secreto, Ubuntu, Mulata, Eco Hotel Las Palmeras and Pao Pao. Accommodation is not included: it is booked directly with the hotel.
- To book an activity departing from the islands, the customer must already have their hotel and tell us which one: pickup is arranged there. If they don't have it yet, they first book the hotel and message us with its name; then we book. If they booked the activity first, the hotel could be cancelled, it could be full, they could forget to tell us or end up departing from Cartagena. If they stay in a house, an Airbnb or a hotel not on our list, they tell us the name and an advisor confirms the pickup before they book and pay: they do not book until then.
- Returning to Cartagena on a different date from the plan is not included. If the guest wants to stay longer on the islands and come back with us another day, a member of our team arranges it (space on the boat, etc.).
- Departure and pickup times are fixed: they cannot be moved earlier or later. If you need an adjustment, a team advisor reviews it.
- Cancellations due to bad weather are unlikely because the Rosario Islands are in sheltered waters. If the Port Authority (Capitanía de Puerto) closes departures to the islands, we first try to reschedule the activity so you don't lose your booking. If rescheduling is not possible, you get a 100% refund. See the terms and conditions: https://divingplanet.org/terminos-y-condiciones/
- Scuba diving is not possible during pregnancy: no mini-course, no dive trips and no courses (DAN and obstetricians advise against it for the whole pregnancy). Surface snorkeling is possible, with her doctor's approval. Whoever comes with her can dive as usual.
- If you get seasick on the boat (the ride to the islands is about 1 hour by speedboat): have a light breakfast before leaving and consider seasickness tablets. If you take any medication, ask your doctor whether you can dive with it.
- We do issue invoices (also to companies). An advisor from our team coordinates the invoice details with the customer.
- There is no maximum age for diving: an older person can dive with the same medical form as everyone else.
- We carry oxygen and a first-aid kit on board, with trained staff, and there is an emergency protocol.
- Groups are small and follow PADI safety standards for each activity.
- The boat is a regular speedboat with no bathroom. On the islands we use the facilities of the hotel where lunch is served: that is where you change, use the bathroom and shower.
- Diving Planet has no parking of its own; there are public car parks in the old town area, and the easiest way to reach the pier is by taxi.
- There is no gift card, but you can book in someone else's name; the date and details are arranged with an advisor.
- Smoking is not allowed on the boat.
- Pets are not allowed on the boat: we go to a National Natural Park.
- Babies and young children who are not yet old enough for any activity (snorkeling starts at 6) can ride the boat with their parents at any age, and they ride free.
- You can bring your own camera on the dives or snorkeling, at your own risk. Diving Planet does not rent cameras.

msg: Tengo el Open Water desde 2019. Mi última inmersión en el mar fue en 2021, pero en septiembre de este año hice el PADI ReActivate en una escuela de Bogotá. ¿Igual tengo que hacer el refresher?
reply:
No, si hiciste el PADI ReActivate en septiembre, cuenta como tu refresher y puedes bucear directamente. 🤿

También necesitas:
• Haber terminado la teoría del curso
• Debes completar la teoría (eLearning) antes de empezar la práctica. Toma aprox. 12 horas y puedes hacerla antes de llegar a la isla.
• Para cursos o minicursos se requiere el formulario médico: https://form.jotform.com/divingplanetcartagena/exoneracion-curso-en-espanol. El enlace se puede enviar junto con el de la reserva; si no lo has completado, te llega otra vez en el correo de confirmación de la reserva. Excepción: el refresher (repaso con instructor) usa el formulario médico de curso, aunque seas buzo certificado.
• Para procesar el seguro, debes completar el formato que te enviamos en el correo de confirmación.
• Después de bucear, esperar mínimo 18 horas antes de tomar un vuelo
• Edad mínima: desde los 10 años.
• Qué llevar: bañador, toalla, crema de sol, gafas de sol y ropa cómoda. El equipo de buceo o de snorkel va incluido en las salidas de buceo, el minicurso, el snorkel y los cursos PADI; en el Divemaster se usa equipo propio.
• Haber completado teoría y piscina en tu centro PADI de origen
• Traer carta/formato de referido firmada por un instructor PADI
• Debes llegar con la teoría y las prácticas en piscina ya completadas en tu centro de origen y traer tu carta de referido firmada por un instructor PADI.
• Para completar la teoría necesitas al menos 4 horas. Debes terminarla antes de empezar la práctica.
• Requisito previo: tener la certificación Open Water.
• Edad mínima: desde los 12 años.
• Para las salidas de buceo recreativo, el refresher y los cursos para buzos ya certificados (Advanced, Rescue, Divemaster y especialidades), debes presentar tu carne de buzo certificado. Puedes enviarnos una foto del carné antes o mostrarlo el día de la actividad.
• Con este plan debes alojarte al menos 1 noche en las Islas del Rosario (hotel no incluido)
• Tras confirmar tu reserva podrás acceder al material/curso digital y completar teoría en PADI eLearning.
• Requisito previo: tener la certificación Advanced Open Water.
• Tener equipo propio
• Tener Open Water, Advanced Open Water y Rescue Diver + EFR vigente (máx. 24 meses)
• Tener buena condición física y saber nadar
• Tener 40 inmersiones registradas para iniciar y 60 al finalizar
• Certificado médico de aptitud para buceo
• La parte práctica solo comienza cuando se completa toda la teoría. El módulo teórico cubre múltiples temas y suele requerir varias sesiones presenciales de refuerzo.
• Requisito previo: tener la certificación Rescue Diver + EFR.
• Edad mínima: desde los 18 años.

¿Y para cuántas personas armamos el plan? 😊
